_comment: Curated lake sets surfaced in the PWA's filter panel ('Collections').
Hand-authored on purpose. These are editorial picks drawn from the reports
in docs/, NOT parsed from them: the reports also list ruled-out lakes,
traps and heavy-pressure waters in prose and tables, and a parser would
sweep those in. Source of truth is this file; the reports are the argument.
Kept OUTSIDE uinta_lakes.db deliberately, like data/app_edits_log.jsonl, so
the seeds / rebuild_database / verify_rebuild machinery stays untouched.
scripts/export_web_data.py reads it, validates every designation against the
database, and nests it into lakes_data.json as `collections`.
Adding a set: append an object with a unique key, a short label (it becomes
a filter chip, so keep it under ~28 chars), the group it sorts under, and
the lakes. `note` is optional per lake and shows on the result card while
that collection is the only one selected.

collections.label: Less-visited: shortlist
collections.description: Tier A. Text, geometry and topo all agree, and there is a real fishery at the end of it.

lakes.note: DWR 2025: "a good lake to visit and be by yourself." 45 ft at 11,200 ft.
The only lake in the database rated Very low pressure. DWR: "one of the most remote lakes in the Uinta River drainage."
Falcon: "Angling pressure is almost nil." Wild brookies, largest lake in Painter Basin.
43 ft and no trail — 3rd-most off-route lake in the range. Best odds of holdover fish out past 2 miles.
DWR: "a remote lake... Fishing pressure is very light." Boulder fields, horse-impossible. Stocked 2026.
DWR 2025: "a good opportunity for anglers seeking solitude." Only 3.5 trail miles — best solitude-per-mile.
The deepest lake in the High Uintas at 147 ft. Splake stocked through 2026, still rated Low pressure.
DWR 2025: "4.2 miles, all of it is cross-country" — the most explicit off-trail line found anywhere.
42.5 acres and 47 ft behind a trailless ridge. Best size-to-solitude ratio in the range.
33 acres, 69 ft, a mile of open tundra off the Highline. CMA notes "the possibility of large fish."
60 ft in a cirque with cliffs "towering a thousand feet." Falcon rates usage Very light.
Falcon: "gets very little usage... sits all by its lonesome." Tales of big, healthy brook trout.
Last 2 miles trailless over open tundra, 10.5 mi from a road. Check rotenone status first.
38 ft at 11,550 ft. A faint trail, a wet meadow, then a steep ravine. No camping.
25 acres and 28 ft in a talus cirque. The crowd stops at Beaver Lake, 3/4 mile short.
45 ft, no trails, "difficult to find" in heavy timber. Lowest of the set at 9,882 ft, so it opens early.

collections.label: Less-visited: strong picks
collections.description: Tier B. Strong evidence, but each carries one caveat — usually road proximity, depth, or an unproven fishery.

lakes.note: The previous pamphlet said "does not sustain fish life." Tigers stocked through 2026.
"lies in an isolated basin and access is difficult." Pair it with BR-43.
DWR: "one of the most inaccessible waters of the Rock Creek drainage." 12.7 mi in.
"Difficult to find without a topographic map... seldom visited." Stocked 2026.
"a remote, seldom visited pond" in a cirque. Approach starts on the Miners Gulch jeep trail.
35 ft. Falcon: "If you feel alone and remote at Milk Lake, it's because, well, you are."
DWR: "ideal for a small group of one to three backpackers who want to get off the beaten trail."
39 ft, "light and limited to day use" — nobody camps there. CMA: larger than normal fish.
20.5 trail miles, the longest walk-in of any light-pressure lake. No Falcon hike goes there.
Half-mile bushwhack; neighbouring Fish Hatchery absorbs the crowd. 17,981 grayling since 2005.
DWR 2025: the trail "disappears in large headwater meadows." 30 ft, cutts and tigers.
Same vanished Middle Fork trail, but it has water and campsites — the basecamp for Bobs.
Genetically pure Colorado River cutthroat, never stocked. Tiny and shallow — go for what the fish are.
9.5 miles into a rugged above-timberline cirque. No campsites, no horse feed. Brookies 2026.
DWR: "seldom visited by anglers." Two off-trail ridge climbs. Not ice-free until mid-July.
35 ft, "surrounded on three sides by talus slides and ledges. Horse access is impossible."
"seldom visited" — the barrier is a 400-foot headwall, not distance. 1.8 miles total.
30 ft, "up a trailless slope" above Swasey Hole, which DWR calls popular and heavily fished.
30 ft, a mile west of Swasey up a rocky timbered slope. No trail, horses difficult.
17 acres, "1 mile through trailless timber," and 10,183 cutthroat stocked — DWR's write-up is stale.
DWR: "This remote natural lake... no clearly defined trails." OSM tags the nearest route "overgrown."
Both approaches are bad on purpose. Grayling, plus leftover goldens from 2014-15.
DWR 1981: "This lake is for anglers who like solitude and ruggedness."
75 ft of wild-brookie water — the DB had it wrong as a 4-acre pond until the 2026-09 fix.
"Horse access is impossible... seldom receives anglers or campers." Grayling and brookies.
18 miles in, then a bushwhacking mile. 21 acres with camping and water — you can base there.
DWR recommends it outright: "avoid the people usually present at the Kidney and Fox lakes."
The pamphlet says it is no longer managed for fishing; DWR has since stocked grayling 7 times.
DWR: "a good choice for anglers seeking solitude." Brand-new grayling in 2026.
"situated in a small, remote basin and is difficult to locate. A topographic map may be helpful."
No trail and a 300-ft wall. Potts: "A good lake for those who are more adventuresome."

collections.label: Undescribed finds
collections.description: Stocked by DWR but described by no pamphlet, book or website. Nobody can plan a trip to a lake no source mentions.

lakes.note: 2.25 mi off any mapped route — 2nd-most off-route lake in the range. Grayling through 2026.
A shelf under Brown Duck Mountain. Stocked five times over twenty years, described by nobody.
Inside the trailless Painter Lakes basin. The most consistently stocked of the undescribed lakes.
A trailless bench in Gilbert Creek Basin, inside the High Uintas Wilderness.
A high pocket near Trail Rider Pass. Close to a trail, but 10 miles from any road.

collections.label: Basin: upper Crow Canyon
collections.description: Dry Gulch. Seven stocked lakes and not one mapped route in the basin. All stocked through 2025-26.

lakes.note: 27 ft — the deepest in the upper chain, so the least likely to winterkill.
DWR: "Angling pressure is very light." Follow the DG-9 inlet a further mile.
DWR: "There is no trail to the lake." Head of the canyon at 11,000 ft.
"very light" pressure. Good fairy shrimp population, but extreme level swings.
100 feet from DG-15, so it costs nothing to fish both. Shallowest of the trio.
The best fishery of the head-of-canyon trio — a large population, partly self-sustaining.
39 ft, the deepest in Dry Gulch. "isolated lake in the head of Heller basin," poorly marked trail.

collections.label: Basin: upper Rasmussen
collections.description: Whiterocks. DWR states outright that there are no maintained trails in this basin. Only 3.5-4.4 miles from a road.

lakes.note: At the very head of the basin. "4.2 miles, all of it is cross-country."
"no trail and both routes are cross country... receives very little fishing pressure." 24 ft.
"very light" pressure. Cutthroat on a reliable 3-year cycle, stocked 2025.
Stocked cutts plus wild brookies moving up from below. A bonus stop en route to Ann.
Wild brookies AND cutthroat, no stocking needed. Meadow shoreline — the fly-casting lake here.
At the toe of a rock glacier. Grayling every three years, stocked 2026.

collections.label: Basin: Painter Lakes
collections.description: Uinta River. The deepest-in cluster in the report — everything here is 9.5-10.7 miles from a drivable road. Falcon: 32.5 miles round trip, usage Light, difficulty High.

lakes.note: The only Very low pressure rating in the database. DWR: most remote in the drainage.
Largest in the basin. Falcon: "Angling pressure is almost nil." Wild brookies.
11.5 acres at 11,037 ft. Brookies stocked through 2022.
The gateway lake — it has the basin's only campsites, so parties stop here.
No write-up in any source, yet stocked with cutthroat six times through 2024.
At the base of Kings Peak in cold, windswept tundra. "a true wilderness experience."
"the lake receives few anglers" — too windy and cold to camp. CMA caught a very large brookie here.
11,740 ft, hidden 150 yards off the trail in its own cirque. DWR: brookies "grow well."

collections.label: Basin: Beaver Lake cirques
collections.description: Beaver Creek. Three off-trail lakes stacked above one busy basecamp. Basecamp at Beaver Lake; everything above it is quiet.

lakes.note: 25.8 acres and 28 ft. "There is no trail to the lake and the terrain is rough."
An eighth of a mile further "up the talus ridge." Grayling water.
18 acres, reached by "an obscure sheep trail... very difficult to locate and follow."

collections.label: Basin: Weyman Lakes
collections.description: Sheep/Carter Creek. Everything past the point where DWR says to leave the horses at Anson Lakes.

lakes.note: "up rock slides and across rough boulder fields... Fishing pressure is very light."
"some of the roughest boulder fields in the Uintas... Even 5 ton boulders can sometimes shift." New grayling 2026.
10 acres at 25 ft. Horse access impossible beyond Anson. Tigers stocked through 2023.
26 ft. Cross-country through downed timber and boulder fields; CMA calls pressure very light.

collections.label: 4x4: go here first
collections.description: Tier 1 — the best measured fish and/or lowest pressure, where the truck genuinely saves a long walk.

lakes.note: Gillnet mean 13.2 in, max 17.7 in / 2 lb — top 3 of 60 samples. 100 yards from the Cliff Lake road end.
Heaviest fish in the entire 2025 DWR survey: an 18.9 in / 4.13 lb brookie. Wild fish.
Gillnet brookies max 18.7 in / 2.96 lb. "Large brook and cutthroat," evening bite.
Pressure Low. Cutts to 17.3 in / 2 lb. FR 235 OHV trail to within ~0.3 mi.
68 acres / 55 ft, "far less angling attention" than its neighbours. The basecamp for the four above.
Pressure Low, wild + stocked grayling, 1990 state-record history. A different species from the rest.
Pressure Low, 23 ft. The Blanchett Park jeep road cuts ~6 mi off the approach; still a rugged trailless 3.5 mi.

collections.label: 4x4: low pressure
collections.description: Tier 2 — low pressure, less hard evidence on fish size.

lakes.note: Pressure Light, 39 ft. Dry Gulch Road "4 tough miles to gate," then 4 mi on foot via Heller.
Pressure Light. Primitive logging road past Jefferson Park, then a 2 mi rim trail.
Pressure Light, 25 ft, essentially unvisited. Miners Gulch jeep trail then 2.5 mi off-trail.
Falcon usage Light. FR 143 logging road end, then 0.5-0.75 mi. Winterkill risk at 12 ft.
Pressure Light. The easiest low-pressure pair on the list, with Survey.
Pressure Low, 27 ft, fresh cutthroat restock after the 2021 rotenone — fish should be growing fast.
Pressure Low, 25 ft, grayling plus leftover goldens. Gardner's Fork jeep road, then 3.5 mi over a steep pass.
Pressure Low, 30 ft. Honest caveat: the 4WD only saves about a mile of a 9-mile trail.
The only Low-pressure lake in the Norway Flats / Spring Canyon cluster. Small fish, pure rock-crawl.

collections.label: 4x4: drive to the water
collections.description: The vehicle reaches the shore or within a couple hundred yards. Mostly busy water — this is the bad-weather / short-day / bring-the-kids set, not a solitude list.

lakes.note: The road ends at a 68-acre, 55-ft lake. Rough: ATV preferred, high-clearance 4WD possible.
About 100 yards from the Cliff Lake road end — and the best gillnet fish of the two.
Road ends at the lake. Brookies to 16.0 in, cutts to 16.5 — but heavy weekend pressure.
Forest Service campground on the shore. Ordinary passenger-car destination.
Drive-to reservoir with campground and guard station. Very heavy recreational use.
Murdock Basin. 44 ft with a large brookie population. JS: "I broke the ball joint on my truck."
The road stops about 100 ft away. "There road is littered with huge rocks."
A 400-480 ft walk from the 4WD road. Pressure high / "excessive."
Same Murdock Basin spur as Hoover. Brookies.
Jeep access, but "Horses cannot be hauled the last 3 miles because of the rugged road."
"a very rough road goes in a short distance." Rainbow catchables, tigers, cutts. Heavy on weekends.
"easily accessible on the Moffit Pass Road." Put-and-take rainbows every year.
Roadside beaver pond off SR-150. The Deadman Traverse is "full of giant rocks that attack your vehicle."
"The last mile of road is passable to 4-wheel drive only." JS: "a strong history of popping tires."
Drive-to via the marked Little Elk turnoff, then north 1/4 mile. Subject to winterkill.
"a side road limited to four-wheel drive vehicles." Brookies, heavy pressure.
Soapstone Basin and Iron Mine roads. 10-12 in rainbows and tigers stocked every year 2021-2026.
